blocks.text: Warning: This article contains references to death by suicide that some readers may find disturbing. As October 7’s third anniversary approaches, Ronen Shalev’s body tells him something’s coming. “You start shivering,” he tells DW. “It’s not just one day and you move on. We have many graves to visit, many families to meet. It’s a difficult time and you feel it in your body.” Both of his children attended the Nova Party in Israel’s south, where almost 400 people were killed in a terrorist attack carried out by Palestinian militant group Hamas and its affiliates in Gaza.
